title: must need may might
name: Must, need to, may, might — Canada.ca
rule: must (law) vs need to (admin) vs may/might (permission) — not “legally required to.” Don’t use can/could for permission (those mean ability).
pass_when: Legal obligation = must; admin = need to; permission = may/might.
fail_when: “Legally required to”; can/could used for permission.
overview: Use must for law, need to for admin, may or might for permission.
apply_when: Wording obligations and permissions in Canada.ca instructional copy.
not_when: Ability statements where can or could correctly means capability.
agent_hint: Write must / need to / may-might; avoid “legally required to” and can-for-permission.
description: Canada.ca distinguishes obligation language carefully: must for law, need to for administrative requirements, and may or might for permission. Do not write “legally required to.” Do not use can or could for permission — those words mean ability, not leave to act. Apply when wording instructional obligations and permissions in Canada.ca copy. Fail “legally required to,” or can/could used where permission is meant.
